sentences.text: Revenue compounded at 4.5% a year from $70.3 billion in FY2016 to $104.8 billion in FY2025 [F1][F10][F205].
The shape is a step change, not a compounding: revenue jumped 19.8% in FY2020 and 13.3% in FY2021, then fell 1.6%, 0.8% and 1.7% in the last three years [D183][D230][D324][D370][D416].
The FY2020 jump came from a 19.3% comparable sales increase as the pandemic shifted spending toward the stores [P51][P55].
The FY2022 collapse in operating margin to 3.5% followed markdowns and excess-inventory costs as discretionary categories slowed [F31][P38].
Food & beverage was the steady grower, rising from 19.6% of revenue in FY2017 to 23.0% in FY2025 [D484][D506].
In FY2025 food & beverage added 0.3pp to revenue growth while apparel subtracted 0.7pp and household essentials subtracted 0.6pp [D508][D565][D515].
FY2025 comparable sales fell 2.6%, split between a 2.2% traffic decline and a 0.4% lower average transaction [P14].
Operating income grew 0.6% a year against 4.5% revenue growth, so there was no operating leverage over the window [F207][F205].
EPS compounded at 6.3% against 3.4% net income growth, the gap coming from a diluted share count that fell from 582.5 million to 455.6 million [F210][F208][X107][X116].
FY2025 operating margin of 4.9% sits below the 5.6% window median and far under the 8.4% FY2021 high [F34][D590][D589].
The FY2025 margin fell 0.3pp, with cost of revenue taking 0.3pp and SG&A adding 0.1pp [D429][D440][D441].
The SG&A rate held at 20.6% only because a 0.6pp interchange settlement benefit offset deleveraging from lower sales [P11].
The largest move was FY2022, when operating margin fell 4.9pp and cost of revenue alone took 4.6pp on markdowns and elevated inventory costs [D290][D301][P38].
Net margin trailed operating margin by 1.3pp in FY2025, with a 22.3% tax rate and $445 million of interest expense [D629][D403][X66].
Operating cash flow was 1.77x net income in FY2025, below the 2.01x window median, and free cash flow was 0.77x net income against a 1.01x median [D404][D619][D405][D599].
The FY2025 operating cash flow decline to $6.56 billion reflected lower net earnings and lower accounts payable leverage [F84][P7].
Free cash flow margin was 2.7%, under the 4.5% median and the 4.2% retail peer median [D401][D596][D611].
Capex rose 28.9% to $3.73 billion, or 1.19x D&A, on more new stores and remodels [D423][F94][D406][P5].
Cash of $5.49 billion against $14.4 billion of long-term debt leaves the company net debt, with a current ratio of 0.94x at the window median [F144][F194][F184][D602].
Return on average equity fell to 24.0%, below the 28.6% retail peer median and the 40th percentile of five peers [D415][D617][D616].
Buybacks plus dividends of $2.46 billion were 86.8% of free cash flow in FY2025, with repurchases cut to $408 million [D412][D413][X126].
Debt issued of $1.98 billion against $1.64 billion repaid lifted long-term debt 3.6% [X150][X160][D427].
Revenue has declined three years running, from $109.1 billion in FY2022 to $104.8 billion in FY2025 [R1][F7][F10].
The current ratio of 0.94x is below 1.0x, though it matches the window median [R2][F184][D602].
Operating margin has fallen two years in a row, by 0.4pp in total, to 4.9% [R4][F32][F34].
The pack's net cash and cash-and-investments figures are unreliable because short-term investments sit inside cash and the current debt portion sits inside long-term debt in early years [R7][R8].
If FY2026 operating margin falls below the FY2025 level of 4.9%, the two-year slide becomes a structural margin problem [F34].
Capex guided at about $5 billion for FY2026 against $3.73 billion in FY2025 would lift capex well above the 3.6% of revenue recorded in FY2025 [P4][F94][D400].
Free cash flow margin recovering above the 4.5% window median would confirm the cash trend has reversed [D596].

failures.sentence: Capex guided at about $5 billion for FY2026 against $3.73 billion in FY2025 would push capex to roughly 4.8% of revenue, above the 3.6% level [P4][F94][D400].
